title: FSC-Certified Custom Packaging: A Buyer’s Verification Guide
seoTitle: FSC Custom Packaging: Buyer Verification Guide | MTT
summary: Check FSC claims for custom boxes and paper bags: label types, supplier certificates, component scope and the documents to confirm before artwork approval.
intro: For FSC-certified custom packaging, verify the proposed supplier, the material claim and the transaction route before approving a logo. A paper sample or a factory certificate alone does not establish what your order can claim. Ask which box or bag components are covered, who will authorise the label and which sales documents will identify the supplied goods. Keep material performance checks separate from certification checks.
cta: Share your box or bag specification, intended FSC claim and purchasing route. MTT can coordinate a review of partner documentation and the material and artwork questions to resolve before sampling.
sections: Choose the claim before choosing the artwork

A buyer may want verified forest sourcing, recycled fibre or a combination of the two. Those are different briefs. FSC describes three label categories; choose the eligible claim from the documented supply route rather than picking whichever logo looks strongest. Source: FSC label explanations.

FSC label meanings and buyer questions
LabelMeaning for the forest-based materialQuestion for your order
FSC 100%Virgin material from FSC-certified forests.Which forest-based components does the approved product claim cover?
FSC MixAn eligible combination of FSC-certified, recycled and/or controlled material.Which claim and labelling system applies to this product?
FSC RecycledVerified recycled forest-based material.Is this the documented product claim, rather than a general recycled-paper description?

These labels are not a percentage statement about every part of a gift set. A magnet, ribbon or foam insert needs its own specification. Do not infer recyclability, compostability or food-contact suitability from an FSC label. The recycled versus recyclable packaging guide addresses that separate design decision.
Verify the holder and the supply route

Use FSC Search to check the organisation name, licence or certificate code and current record. Match the holder to the actual proposed manufacturing site and relevant scope. Save the dated result with the quotation documents; an old certificate screenshot can be a useful lead but should not be the end of verification.

FSC chain of custody concerns the material’s passage through the supply chain. Identify who manufactures, takes legal ownership, invoices and makes the claim. A certified production partner does not automatically extend its certificate to an independent trading or development company. Source: FSC chain of custody.

MTT’s partner-based production model makes this handoff worth resolving early. Before an FSC claim is promised, the applicable certificate holder should confirm the proposed transaction and labelling route. Do not assume an MTT invoice can carry a certified claim simply because the source factory holds a certificate.
Break a rigid box or paper bag into components

Start with a bill of materials. For a wrapped rigid box, separate structural board, outer wrap, inner lining and the insert. For a paper bag, separate body paper, reinforcement cards, handles and any decorative attachments. Record the proposed material supplier and claim for each relevant component.

An order-level evidence sheet
ItemRecord before approvalReason to pause
Outer wrap and boardMaterial grade, intended claim and covered product scope.The quotation names only the wrapping paper.
Insert and liningMaterial identity and whether included in the claim.The insert changes after the label was approved.
Label artworkApproved label, code, product scope and responsible holder.A designer copies a logo from another brand.
Sales documentationWhich entity supplies the claim and how it identifies the goods.The certificate and seller names do not reconcile.

This is a purchasing worksheet, not an FSC audit checklist. Ask the certificate holder or its certification body to resolve uncertain eligibility. Do not improvise a partial-product claim to fit an attractive package design.
Test the chosen material as packaging

Certification does not select board stiffness, folding behaviour or print appearance. If a specified paper changes, compare the actual replacement using the approved structure and finish. A recycled paper option can be suitable, but its colour, texture and forming behaviour still need approval for that design.

For a perfume rigid box, inspect wrapped corners, visible lining and insert fit after the proposed material substitution. For a shopping bag, agree the loaded configuration and handle checks. Keep those findings with the material reference. Use the material selection guide and sampling workflow to define the physical approval.

Illustrative scenario: a brand approves a pale wrap and later selects a darker recycled stock. Retain the sourcing requirement, but reopen colour and foil approval on the new stock. The earlier visual sample is no longer an adequate reference for the changed surface.
Release the claim and the packaging together

Before printing, reconcile the final bill of materials, holder verification, approved label file and purchase documentation. Name the person who can release artwork. Any later change of paper, site, supplier or invoicing route should trigger a claim review as well as a production review.

FSC distinguishes promotional trademark use from applying labels to products. A promotional licence does not itself permit a company to label products. Source: FSC promotional use guidance.

At delivery, check that the documents refer to the actual goods and quantities supplied. Keep the evidence with the reorder specification. This creates a usable purchasing record instead of a folder of logos that nobody can connect to the finished order.
Sources and evidence boundaries

Prepared by MTT Packaging editorial. Sources checked on 8 October 2026.

  • FSC: the three label categories
  • FSC: chain of custody
  • FSC Search: certification and licensing records
  • FSC: promotional use and product labelling

title: GMI Printing Certification: Build a Packaging Colour Approval Brief
seoTitle: GMI Printing & Packaging Colour Control | MTT
summary: Turn a GMI printing requirement into a packaging approval brief: verify the print site, colour reference, measurement method, finish and reorder controls.
intro: If your packaging brief requires GMI, confirm the exact printer and the customer programme before approving production. Then define the physical colour reference, substrate, finish and measurement conditions for the job. A facility credential cannot replace an agreed artwork and colour approval. For a coordinated box-and-bag range, approve each material separately and compare the finished components together.
cta: Send the retailer’s print requirements, brand colour reference and the box-and-bag components you need. MTT can coordinate partner scope checks and a practical colour approval brief.
sections: Start with the printer and programme identity

GMI refers here to Graphic Measures International in packaging print qualification. A publicly available GMI-issued recognition letter refers to a designated programme’s approved print-supplier matrix. It is a historical example of programme-linked qualification, not evidence about MTT or its partners’ current status. Source: GMI-issued recognition letter, hosted by MM Group.

Ask the buying team which programme and current requirements apply. Obtain the proposed site’s current evidence and verify acceptance through the programme owner or customer. Match the manufacturing address and printing process to the job. Do not treat another site’s certificate, or a supplier website logo, as sufficient approval.

This guide does not reproduce a current GMI scoring manual or prescribe programme pass marks. Public historical material is insufficient for those claims. If a retailer mandates a specific approved source, settle that requirement before treating a quotation as production-ready.
Write the colour reference so two suppliers can use it

“Match our brand green” needs a controlled reference. Record the artwork revision, spot or process-colour specification, approved physical sample, substrate and finish. State whether the comparison is made before or after coating. A phone image is useful for discussion, but its appearance depends on capture, screen and viewing conditions.

A useful reference pack contains a labelled retained sample and a written measurement brief. The parties should agree the colour-difference formula, instrument setup, measurement conditions, locations and acceptance limits. X-Rite explains colour tolerances as an agreed boundary around a target, with different calculation methods affecting how differences are evaluated. Source: X-Rite colour tolerancing white paper.

Do not copy a universal Delta E threshold from a marketing page. The customer’s programme, materials and approved appearance determine the acceptable limits. Do not compare results from different methods as if the numbers were interchangeable.
Separate print variables from finishing variables

Colour approval fields for a custom packaging job
ControlWhat to agreeWhat can otherwise go wrong
ReferenceIdentified master, artwork revision and approval date.Printer matches an obsolete sample.
SubstrateActual paper grade, colour and surface.The same artwork looks different on the bag and box.
MeasurementFormula, instrument conditions, locations and limits.Two apparently similar reports cannot be compared.
FinishCoating, lamination or foil and when to judge appearance.Unfinished sheets pass but finished packs disappoint.
ReleaseApprover, exceptions and retained production reference.An informal photograph becomes the supposed master.

For a luxury rigid box, the visible surface may be a wrapped speciality paper rather than the structural board. Evaluate the printed wrap and then the assembled pack. On a folding carton, include folds, solid areas and small text in the visual review. Neither a colour reading nor a facility credential answers whether the crease, glue seam or insert works.

The printing and finishing guide separates process selection from appearance approval. For metallic decoration, also use matching gold foil across a box and paper bag.
Approve a coordinated set under one comparison plan

Illustrative scenario: a perfume launch combines a wrapped rigid box and a paper bag. Both use a dark blue graphic. Their paper surfaces differ, and the bag has a different protective finish. Matching the ink recipe alone is not an adequate approval instruction.

Have each proposed print route produce a representative sample. Review the two finished components side by side under agreed conditions, then record any accepted difference. If the brand requires an especially close visual match, discuss material and finish alignment before repeated colour corrections. A substrate change may solve more than another artwork adjustment.

Keep the comparison set intact. Sending the box to one supplier and the bag to another without a shared reference invites two locally acceptable but visibly mismatched results. A retained paired set gives the buyer a clearer basis for reorder approval.
Carry the approval into production and reorders

Record the site, process, material grade, artwork version, colour reference and finishing specification in the released brief. Ask the printer to retain the agreed measurement and visual records with the identified production lot. Any reported deviation should identify the affected component and decision owner.

Define when a change needs renewed approval: paper substitution, press route, coating, artwork, foil or manufacturing site. See reorder specification change control for recording those decisions. Where a customer programme applies, its change rules take precedence over an informal “same as last time” instruction.

MTT can coordinate the packaging brief and partner handoffs. Current programme acceptance remains a matter for the actual printer and relevant customer or programme authority. Shipment release should also include the separate structural and workmanship checks in the packaging inspection checklist.
Sources and evidence boundaries

Prepared by MTT Packaging editorial. Sources checked on 8 October 2026.

  • GMI-issued letter: historical programme-linked supplier qualification example
  • X-Rite: colour difference and tolerancing methods

title: ISO Certification for Packaging Suppliers: What Buyers Should Verify
seoTitle: ISO Packaging Supplier Verification Guide | MTT
summary: Verify a packaging supplier’s ISO standard, certificate scope, site and status, then connect quality-system evidence to samples, changes and shipment approval.
intro: An ISO logo does not tell you which standard, production site or activity has been certified. Request the actual certificate, verify its current status and compare its scope with your packaging order. If the requirement is a quality management system, identify the applicable standard and edition explicitly. Keep product testing, sample approval and shipment inspection as separate requirements.
cta: Share your supplier qualification requirement and packaging specification. MTT can coordinate the relevant production partner’s documents and identify the quality records your order needs.
sections: Identify the standard instead of accepting “ISO certified”

ISO develops standards; external certification bodies issue certificates. ISO itself does not certify a factory, and its logo is not a generic certification mark available for supplier advertising. Source: ISO certification guidance.

For a quality-management requirement, buyers often refer to ISO 9001. Other management standards address different subjects. Read the exact standard and edition on the proposed partner’s evidence instead of assuming that a familiar logo means quality, environmental, safety and product approval all at once.

This article does not identify a particular ISO standard as held by every MTT production partner. That information must come from the relevant partner’s current documents. Where an edition is in transition, ask the certification body to confirm the certificate’s status and applicable transition arrangements; do not guess from the publication date of a newer standard.
Check the organisation, site and scope together

Supplier certificate verification worksheet
FieldBuyer checkPractical question
Legal holderMatch the company named in the supply arrangement.Who actually operates the proposed production site?
SiteCheck the address and any site annex.Is this job made at the site covered by the evidence?
Standard and editionRecord the exact designation.Does it satisfy our contractual requirement?
Certified scopeRead the activities and exclusions.Does it cover the packaging work being proposed?
Status and issuerVerify with the issuer or appropriate database.Is the certificate active and is the issuer identifiable?

ISO points buyers to IAF CertSearch or the relevant certification and accreditation bodies for verification of accredited certification. Source: ISO verification guidance.

Keep the certificate and verification date in the supplier file. A matching group name is not enough if the scope describes a different activity. If assembly or finishing is subcontracted, ask how that work is controlled and which site performs it. Record unresolved questions before placing an order that depends on a specific qualification.
Translate a quality system into order records

A quality-management-system certificate should not be presented as certification of the individual box or proof that every delivered item is defect-free. ISO’s expected-outcomes guidance distinguishes system certification from product certification. Source: ISO/IAF expected outcomes for ISO 9001 certification.

The useful buying question is how the proposed partner will control your specification. Ask for the records that link the commercial order to the physical reference: drawing revision, artwork revision, material identity, approved sample, exceptions and release responsibility. The packaging brief guide helps assemble the inputs.

For a rigid box, identify the approved internal dimensions and insert geometry. For a folding carton, include the closure and packing method. An attractive sample with no revision reference is harder to reproduce or investigate than a controlled sample with clear acceptance notes.
Use one change scenario to test the handoff

Illustrative scenario: a skincare brand approves a carton and insert for one pump bottle. Before the reorder, the bottle supplier changes the pump collar. The outside carton still looks correct, but the product may no longer fit as approved.

Ask how the proposed production team would detect the changed input, assess it and obtain approval. The answer should identify the new product dimensions or sample, the revised insert drawing and the person who releases the change. It should not rely only on a previous purchase order or a certificate on the wall.

MTT’s role can include coordinating that product-to-packaging handoff with the manufacturing partner. The sampling process establishes the new reference, while reorder change control records what changed. Keep commercial approval and technical approval identifiable even if one person performs both.
Ask what happens when a lot does not meet the brief

Before shipment, agree the inspection scope, defect definitions and release authority. Ask how an affected lot is identified and held, what evidence supports sorting or rework, and who can accept a concession. Certification does not choose those order-specific limits for the buyer.

If a repeated problem occurs, a useful corrective-action response explains the cause, the affected goods, the action taken and the check showing whether the action worked. A replacement sample alone does not explain why the production problem happened. Avoid demanding a generic “zero defects” promise that nobody has translated into measurable requirements.

Use the production inspection checklist alongside supplier qualification. Together, the two records answer different questions: whether the proposed supplier meets the required system qualification, and whether the identified shipment meets the agreed order criteria.
Sources and evidence boundaries

Prepared by MTT Packaging editorial. Sources checked on 8 October 2026.

  • ISO: certification, issuer identity and verification
  • ISO/IAF: expected outcomes and limits of ISO 9001 certification

title: Does Custom Packaging Need CE Marking? An Artwork Approval Guide
seoTitle: CE Marking on Custom Packaging: Buyer Guide | MTT
summary: Understand when CE marking belongs on product packaging, who supplies approved compliance artwork and what to check before printing cartons or gift boxes.
intro: An ordinary empty paper box or shopping bag does not need CE marking merely because it is packaging. CE applies to products covered by specific EU legislation. When a mark is required on the packaged product, whether it also appears on packaging depends on the applicable rules. Obtain product-specific instructions from the responsible manufacturer before printing, and keep those instructions linked to the correct SKU and artwork revision.
cta: Share the product category, target market and compliance-approved artwork instructions. MTT can review how the required information fits the packaging structure before print approval.
sections: Separate the product obligation from the empty box

The EU explains that CE marking is mandatory only for products covered by legislation requiring it, and must not be used on other products. It is not a general quality award for a packaging supplier. Source: Your Europe, CE marking.

A carton for an electrical device and an ordinary cosmetic gift box may have different labelling requirements because of what they contain. Do not transfer a CE symbol from one project to another simply because the same factory prints both. A factory’s equipment documentation also does not establish that its empty boxes are CE-certified.

Start by identifying the product and applicable legislation with the responsible compliance team. If the packaging itself incorporates a regulated function or is supplied as a different kind of product, that classification needs its own assessment. This article addresses artwork coordination, not a conformity assessment for a particular product.
Get the compliance decision before designing the panel

The responsible product manufacturer should provide the approved marking instructions and supporting product identification. The EU Blue Guide explains the responsibilities and conformity-marking framework; the product-specific legislation determines the detailed obligations. Source: European Commission Blue Guide, 2022.

Packaging artwork handoff for regulated products
InputWho should confirm itPackaging action
Product and SKUResponsible product manufacturer or compliance team.Match the artwork to the exact product identity.
Applicable markingResponsible compliance team.Place only the approved marks and accompanying information.
Placement and sizeApplicable product rules and approved instructions.Check the flat layout and assembled pack.
Languages and identifiersResponsible market-compliance owner.Reserve sufficient readable space.
Final releaseNamed authorised artwork approver.Record the approved version before printing.

This handoff does not transfer the manufacturer’s legal duties to the printer. MTT can coordinate the dieline, sample and production artwork; it should not invent a CE declaration or decide that a customer’s product meets technical requirements.
Check minimum size without treating it as a universal layout rule

Your Europe states a general minimum CE-marking height of 5 mm unless the relevant product rules provide otherwise. The proportions must be maintained. It also explains that packaging or accompanying documents may be used where product placement is not possible, subject to the applicable requirements. Source: EU marking and placement guidance.

Measure the final artwork at its actual print size. Do not stretch the symbol to fill a narrow panel or assume that printing it on the box always replaces marking the product. Confirm any required accompanying identification separately; the presence of a notified body in a process does not justify adding an arbitrary number.

A printer’s proof should show scale and panel position. After folding or wrapping, check that a seam, sleeve, closure or label does not hide required information. For a drawer box, decide which surface remains accessible in the product’s supplied configuration. These are practical artwork checks, not substitutes for the applicable legal placement rule.
Avoid the wrong-SKU failure

Illustrative scenario: a brand sells two similar gift sets, one containing an electronic accessory and one containing only non-electrical items. The design team duplicates the first carton file for the second. A copied compliance panel may now describe the wrong product or carry an inapplicable mark.

Use a product-to-artwork matrix rather than approving by appearance alone. Record SKU, contents, language version, compliance instruction, dieline revision and artwork file. Mark obsolete versions clearly and prevent them from returning to the print queue. If several products share one outer box, confirm the approved way to distinguish the supplied configurations.

The shared-box planning guide covers the structural side of a multi-SKU range. The same efficiency goal must be checked against each product’s information requirements before the artwork is shared.
Approve the physical proof and keep the record

Review required text and marks on a representative assembled sample, not only on a flat screen. Check legibility, placement, correct identifiers and whether any added sleeve or sticker changes what the buyer sees. Preserve the approved file and instructions with the order.

The packaging sampling process provides the physical approval stage. Use artwork and specification change control if product contents, market, language or responsible-party information changes.

Other packaging requirements still need their own assessment. CE is not a shortcut for material restrictions, environmental claims or packaging-waste obligations. The PPWR packaging guide discusses a separate EU packaging topic. Ask the responsible compliance owner to confirm current requirements for the actual product and market before release.
Sources and evidence boundaries

Prepared by MTT Packaging editorial. Sources checked on 8 October 2026.

  • European Union: CE marking scope, dimensions and placement
  • European Commission: Blue Guide on EU product rules, 2022

title: Sedex and SMETA for Packaging Suppliers: A Buyer’s Audit Guide
seoTitle: Sedex & SMETA Packaging Supplier Audit Guide | MTT
summary: Check Sedex membership, SMETA audit scope, site identity and corrective actions when selecting packaging production partners for a responsible sourcing programme.
intro: Sedex membership and a SMETA audit are different forms of evidence. Membership alone does not establish that a packaging factory has completed an audit, and SMETA is not a product certification or a pass/fail guarantee. Review the actual site, audit date, scope, findings and corrective actions against your sourcing policy. Confirm that the proposed production and any subcontracted work match the evidence you reviewed.
cta: Share your responsible-sourcing policy, required audit scope and packaging process. MTT can coordinate the relevant partner’s document review and clarify production-site and subcontracting questions.
sections: Ask for the audit record behind the logo

Sedex provides a platform for supply-chain information; SMETA is its social-audit methodology. Sedex describes SMETA as a tool for identifying conditions and improvements, not a certification with a pass or fail. Source: Sedex SMETA overview.

A membership reference can help identify an organisation, but it does not answer when a particular factory was audited or which findings remain open. Ask for authorised access to the applicable report and corrective-action information. Keep the site identity, scope and review date together.

For MTT’s partner-based production, the evidence belongs to the relevant manufacturing partner. It should not be described as “MTT Sedex certification.” Nor should one partner’s record be used as a blanket claim about every site that might make a box, bag or insert.
Choose the scope your buying policy needs

SMETA offers 2-pillar and 4-pillar assessments. The two founding pillars are labour standards and health and safety; the 2-pillar scope also includes a basic environmental assessment. The 4-pillar scope expands environmental assessment and includes business ethics. Source: Sedex Complete SMETA Audit Guide.

Audit scope questions for packaging buyers
EvidenceWhat it helps establishWhat still needs review
Sedex membershipAn organisation’s platform participation.Whether the proposed site has the required audit evidence.
SMETA 2-pillarLabour and health-and-safety review, with basic environmental assessment.Whether this scope meets the buyer’s sourcing policy.
SMETA 4-pillarBroader environmental and business-ethics coverage as well.Actual findings, corrective actions and site relevance.
Corrective-action recordsActions taken or planned in response to findings.Closure evidence and any buyer-specific follow-up.

A larger scope is not a claim that no problems exist. Read the findings. If your customer specifies an audit scope, date range or approval process, obtain those requirements before offering a production site. There is no universal buyer acceptance rule in this article.
Match the audit boundary to the production route

Map the main operations for the order: printing, cutting, wrapping or gluing, insert production, bag-handle fitting, assembly and packing. Ask which operations occur at the reviewed site and which are subcontracted. A box can pass through several businesses before shipment.

The risk is a paperwork mismatch: a report names the main factory, while labour-intensive assembly is carried out elsewhere. Do not assume the audit automatically covers that other site. Ask the partner to identify the arrangement and refer it to the buyer’s sourcing team for the necessary review.

This mapping can sit beside the material and process specification in the packaging brief. Record the production route before a tight launch schedule makes changing it difficult. Where a new site is proposed, revisit the approval instead of treating the old report as transferable.
Review corrective actions as decisions, not a badge

Sedex explains that approved audit companies conduct SMETA and that corrective-action planning supports improvement. Source: Sedex audit process.

For each relevant finding, ask what action was agreed, who owns it, its due date and what evidence shows progress or closure. The responsible auditor and buying organisation determine the applicable verification and acceptance process. Avoid converting a report into an unsupported “100% ethical” claim.

Handle worker-related information through authorised channels. A public blog or product page should not publish confidential audit detail, personal records or a customer’s internal supplier decision. Public marketing can explain the verification process without exposing the report.

Illustrative scenario: a seasonal gift-box order requires extra assembly capacity. The proposed partner offers an additional assembly site. Before accepting the schedule, check whether that site and arrangement meet the buyer’s policy. An earlier audit of the original site does not resolve the new handoff by itself.
Keep social due diligence separate from product quality

A social audit does not establish colour accuracy, box compression performance, insert fit or food-contact suitability. Those questions need their own specifications and evidence. Combining them into one “certified factory” statement makes it harder for a buyer to see what has actually been checked.

Use the packaging inspection checklist for lot acceptance and the sampling process for structure and appearance approval. Social-audit evidence belongs in the supplier qualification file, linked to the approved production route.

Before reordering, check whether the site, ownership, audit status or subcontracting route has changed. Let the buyer’s policy define the required review interval and escalation rules. MTT can coordinate documents and production handoffs, while the buying organisation retains its own supplier-acceptance decision.
Sources and evidence boundaries
